headline: Bengals 31, Dolphins 24

body.label: Turning points
body.text: Cincinnati converted an 81-yard opening kickoff return into a touchdown. Two second-quarter Malik Willis interceptions helped create a 21–7 halftime deficit. Miami later rallied to 28–18, but Willis’ lost fumble at his own 10-yard line effectively ended the comeback.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Ollie Gordon II rushed for 88 yards and a touchdown. Willis added 74 rushing yards, one passing score and one rushing score, while rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. caught his first NFL touchdown.

body.label: Injuries
body.text: Cornerback Julius Brents left with a stinger and did not return. De’Von Achane remains on season-ending injured reserve.

body.label: Takeaway
body.text: Miami produced season highs in total offense (331 yards), rushing (217) and points, but three quarterback turnovers and another damaging special-teams play erased that progress.

next: Bye on October 18; at the New York Jets on Sunday, October 25, at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS.

hurricanes.headline: Bye week

body.label: Roster/injury news
body.text: Coach Mario Cristobal said defensive end Marquise Lightfoot and starting cornerback Xavier Lucas are fully recovered. Linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. and cornerback Damari Brown are also healthy. Starting right guard Max Buchanan remains out, with Cristobal hopeful he can return later this season.

body.label: Takeaway
body.text: The week off was especially valuable for a battered defense. Regaining Lightfoot and Lucas strengthens Miami’s pass rush and secondary ahead of its rivalry game, although Buchanan’s absence creates a significant offensive-line adjustment.

hurricanes.next: Florida State at Miami on Saturday, October 17, at 7:00 p.m. ET on ESPN.
